Pupil dilation when listening in quiet and in noise

Source: R/data.R
pupil_noise.Rd

Pupil size over 3 seconds after stimulus onset, 12 trials per condition from each of 24 participants. Listening in noise leads to a larger and later peak. For GAMMs with autocorrelated residuals.

Usage

pupil_noise

Format

A tibble with 17856 rows and 6 columns:

participant

P01 to P24.

condition

"quiet" or "noise".

trial

Trial number within condition, 1 to 12.

trial_id

One level per trial (participant.condition.trial).

time

Time from stimulus onset in ms, 0 to 3000 in steps of 100.

pupil

Baseline-corrected pupil size, arbitrary units.

Source

data-raw/pupil_noise.R

Details

True model: a gamma-shaped response peaking at 180 units after 1200 ms in quiet, and 90 units higher and 250 ms later in noise. The peak shrinks by 4 units per trial (habituation). By-participant variation in peak (SD 40), latency (SD 150 ms) and noise effect (SD 30); by-trial variation in peak (SD 40) and baseline (SD 15); residuals are AR(1) with rho 0.8 and SD 12.

Examples

head(pupil_noise)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 6
#>   participant condition trial trial_id     time pupil
#>   <fct>       <fct>     <int> <fct>       <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 P01         noise         1 P01.noise.1     0   5.2
#> 2 P01         noise         1 P01.noise.1   100  -1  
#> 3 P01         noise         1 P01.noise.1   200   1.8
#> 4 P01         noise         1 P01.noise.1   300  20.1
#> 5 P01         noise         1 P01.noise.1   400  55.6
#> 6 P01         noise         1 P01.noise.1   500  84.4
